1: I am afraid that sooner or later I will lose the people who keep me going in sport.
2: When the coach changes, it takes me a long time to find my feet.
3: I lack the certainty that someone will back me even in a bad spell.
4: When the coach pays me no attention for a few days, I look for what I did wrong.
5: In the team I quickly attach myself to one person.
6: I am afraid that once I stop performing, everyone's interest will vanish.
7: When a teammate I was attached to leaves, it throws me more than it should.
8: I need to hear that the coach is counting on me more often than the others do.
9: When the end of the season or of my contract approaches, I cannot think about anything else.
10: I would rather keep my distance than risk being dropped again.
11: I expect the people in the team to take advantage of me sooner or later.
12: I am most careful around those closest to me.
13: When someone in the team praises me, I look for the ulterior motive.
14: I ration what I say about myself so that it cannot be used against me.
15: I feel my place in the line-up is decided behind my back.
16: I would rather show hardness first than have someone show it to me.
17: I read the coach's disagreement as an attack rather than as a work matter.
18: I watch who the coach favours.
19: When two teammates talk quietly, it occurs to me that it is about me.
20: Trusting anyone in the team completely feels risky to me.
21: I feel nobody really knows what this sport costs me.
22: I lack someone I can talk to about how I really am.
23: The people around me are interested in my result, not in me.
24: Even among teammates I feel alone.
25: Nobody asks me how I felt after the match.
26: I cannot ask for support, even when I need it.
27: When someone offers me help, it makes me uncomfortable.
28: I choose people who cannot reach emotionally as far as I need them to.
29: After a good performance I feel emptiness rather than joy.
30: I feel I have to be strong even when I am not.
31: In the dressing room I feel I do not belong there.
32: The others seem to have it easier among themselves.
33: In the team I am an observer rather than part of the group.
34: I do not feel like joining team activities outside training.
35: I feel different from the rest of the team.
36: In a large group I stay quiet even when I have something to say.
37: If I left from one day to the next, nobody would miss me.
38: In a new squad it takes me a long time to feel at home.
39: I feel the team only takes me on my performance.
40: At camps and squad gatherings I feel most out of place.
41: Without an instruction from the coach I make worse decisions on the pitch.
42: I could not put a training plan together on my own.
43: When I have to decide quickly, my eyes search for the bench.
44: After making my own decision in play, I doubt for a long time whether it was right.
45: I need someone to confirm that I did it well.
46: Changes in the training plan unsettle me until someone explains them to me.
47: Without the coach at the session I get less work done.
48: I feel the others know better than I do what I should be doing.
49: I would rather leave responsibility for decisions in play to the more experienced.
50: I will not accept help even when I need it, because I would feel incapable.
51: Before a performance, scenarios of it ending badly come into my head.
52: I am more afraid of injury than is usual in my sport.
53: I monitor every ache in my body for whether it means something serious.
54: After coming back from injury I unconsciously avoid the same movement.
55: Travelling to competitions I think about everything that could happen.
56: I am afraid of losing control at the decisive moment.
57: When nothing bad happens for a long time, I expect it is still to come.
58: I would rather go around a risk in play, even when taking it would pay off.
59: I am afraid of losing my sporting career from one day to the next.
60: I choose the safe option even when I know it leads to defeat.
61: If the people in the team got to know me better, they would stop respecting me.
62: I hide parts of myself from my teammates.
63: After a mistake I feel ashamed long after the match is over.
64: Praise slides off me; criticism sticks.
65: I feel that at heart I am worse than I appear.
66: Compared with my teammates I feel less worthy as a person, not as a player.
67: I avoid situations that would show what I am really like.
69: When someone respects me, I feel they are mistaken about me.
70: I am afraid it will come out one day that I do not have the character for this.
71: Compared with people my age I have fallen behind.
72: I go into a match assuming it probably will not work out.
73: Success, when it comes, does not feel like mine.
74: I am afraid people will find out I am not as good as they think.
75: I do not go all in on situations where I could fail.
76: I would rather lower my goals than fail to meet them.
77: When things are going well, I wait for it to end.
78: I got to my level more by circumstance than anything else.
79: After a setback I confirm to myself that I expected it anyway.
80: I do not believe I will improve significantly any more.
81: I say yes even when I know I cannot manage it.
82: I only disagree with the coach in my head.
83: In the team I set my own needs aside automatically.
84: When I do get my way, I feel guilty.
85: I train even when my body is telling me it is too much.
86: I am afraid that if I say no, I will lose my place.
87: I adapt to someone else's style of play even when it does not suit me.
88: I bottle up anger and it comes out somewhere else.
89: I would rather say nothing about pain or fatigue.
90: I do what my parents or the club expect of me, not what I want.
91: Second place is not a result for me.
92: Even after a good performance I mainly see the mistakes.
93: I have to earn my rest.
94: When I ease off, I feel everyone notices immediately.
95: I demand more of myself than the coach does.
96: A day off makes me nervous.
97: I fuss over details of preparation even when they add nothing more.
98: Joy in a performance lasts only briefly, then the next bar goes up.
99: I never feel it was enough.
100: If I am not the best at what matters to me, it is worth nothing to me.
101: I cannot stand being contradicted by the coach.
102: I get angry when I do not get the playing time I believe is mine.
103: The rules that apply to the team fit me less well.
104: When something restricts me, I react more sharply than necessary.
105: I only finish a boring session by forcing myself.
106: I find it hard to put off pleasure for the sake of a distant goal.
107: Waiting my turn does not come easily to me.
108: I take criticism as an attack on my standing.
109: When something stops being enjoyable, seeing it through is a problem.
110: I expect to be accommodated more than the others.
